name: US state paid family and medical leave (PFML) program requirements for employers
description: Contribution rates, employer/employee splits, employee-count thresholds, benefit durations, wage replacement formulas, and maximum weekly benefits for every US state that mandates paid family and medical leave. Each record is one state's PFML program, stating the current payroll contribution rate, who pays what share, when the program took effect, and the key compliance numbers an employer needs. Answers 'does my state require paid family leave', 'what is the PFML contribution rate in [state]', and 'how many weeks of paid leave do employees get in [state]'.
licence: Facts extracted from state government PFML program pages; contribution rates and benefit rules are statutory and not copyrightable

All businesses with at least one qualified employee are required to register with the FAMLI Division in My FAMLI+ Employer. Self-employed individuals, or sole proprietors with no employees, are not required to register. Regardless of your business structure, if you have at least one qualifying employee, you need to register with the FAMLI Division, submit wage data and send in premiums on behalf of that employee. Visit our <https://famli.colorado.gov/individuals-and-families> Individuals and Families page for more information on the options for self-employed individuals. The law applies to private employers with 50 or more employees. The FMLA also allows states to set standards that are more expansive than the federal law and many states have chosen to do so. In response to the COVID-19 pandemic, many states have enacted or expanded family leave permanently.
